decision: Adopt the OpenHands v0.54.0 function-calling tool schema verbatim instead of designing one. The project rule is that a tool protocol, a data-generation method, a reward scheme and an optimiser are not all invented at once; this manifest removes the protocol from that list.
why_this_protocol: It is a real, widely used protocol rather than this project's design.

Real multi-turn trajectories exist in exactly this format: nebius/SWE-rebench-openhands-trajectories, cc-by-4.0, 32161 successful trajectories over 1823 repositories, OpenHands v0.54.0, function calling.
Qwen3-8B's own chat template renders tools natively (verified: the template contains a tools branch and <tool_call>/<tool_response> markers).
The upstream veRL SWE-agent recipe uses a subprocess plus text proxy, which forces re-tokenisation; adopting a function-calling schema lets the agent loop stay token-in/token-out.

source.note: huggingface.co is unreachable from this project's machines; hf-mirror.com is reachable and served this file. The dataset sha above comes from the mirror's dataset API, not from a signed manifest.

tools.name: execute_bash
tools.role: run one bash command in a persistent shell session inside the task container

tools.name: think
tools.role: log a thought, no side effect

tools.name: finish
tools.role: signal task completion; terminates the episode

tools.name: task_tracker
tools.role: optional structured task list; no repository side effect

adopted_subset.reason: The first four are the ones the environment must actually execute. task_tracker is pure bookkeeping and can be admitted or dropped without changing what the sandbox does; the choice must be recorded per experiment because it changes the action space.

consequences_for_this_project: The old restricted 7-action JSON protocol (list_files/search_text/read_file/replace_text/replace_lines/run_tests/finish) is NOT the new route's protocol. It stays in the tree, frozen, and is never mixed with this one.

`execute_bash` requires a real shell inside the task container. The container already runs with --network none, --cap-drop ALL, --pids-limit, memory and CPU caps and no host mounts, so the shell is confined to the task container.

Because the agent can now write anywhere including the verifier's test files, correctness can no longer be enforced by a read-only guard on those paths. The reward must instead be computed the way SWE-bench does it: extract the agent's patch, apply it together with the official test patch to a clean checkout, and grade there. Blocking edits was the wrong mechanism; grading on a clean tree is the right one.

The old guards (read-before-edit, duplicate-action refusal, premature-finish refusal) must NOT be carried over: the A/B/C audit showed they caused 10 of 18 first failures, and they would put the RL action distribution out of line with the SFT trajectories, which were produced without them.
unverified: The exact `system`/`instance`/`next-step` prompt templates used by OpenHands v0.54.0 are NOT in tools.json. They must be read from the trajectory rows themselves before SFT rendering is written.
Whether Qwen3-8B emits this schema reliably under the pinned template has not been tested on a GPU.
The observations' exact text layout (truncation markers, exit-code framing) has not been inspected in a real row yet.
